terms.gloss: a supply, a stock, plenty (of something)
evidence: Caes. BC 1.49: exercitus omnium rērum abundābat cōpiā (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Sen. 71: bonōrum memoria et cōpia
terms.comment: With the genitive of what there is a supply of; in the plural, cōpiae, supplies and resources (see resources).

terms.gloss: supplies, provisions (for an army or a journey)
evidence: Caes. BG 2.9: commeātū nostrōs prohibēre (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Traupman: used both as a collective singular and in the plural.

phrases.latin: frūctus autem senectūtis est, ut saepe dīxī, ante partōrum bonōrum memoria et cōpia
phrases.english: the harvest of old age, as I have often said, is the memory and the store of good things gathered before
to cut the enemy off from their supplies
phrases.source: Traupman 188; cf. Liv. 26.39.10: commeātūs hostibus (Lewis & Short s.v. interclūdō)

sources: Lewis & Short: copia · Lewis & Short: commeatus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 188, 388.
